lawyer: Md. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate for Md. Jamiruddin Sircar, Advocate ----- for petitioners. No One ----- for the opposite party.
parties:
Kamal Anwar & ors.
Vs.
Muhammad Kabir Khan
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J.:- This Rule obtained under Section 115 C.P.C. is directed against the Order dated 26-6-76 passed by Mr. N.I. Khan, Munsif, Faridpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 191 of 1976. Late poet Jasimuddin as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.4 of 1974 against the Opposite party as defendant before the Sadar Munsif Faridpur praying for a decree of ejectment from the suit premises. During the pendency of the said suit poet Jasimuddin died on 14-3-76 leaving behind the 7 petitioners as his legal heirs who are sui juris. 

 2. The suit was fixed for hearing on 6-4-76. On that date Mr. Md. Sakhawat Hossain, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff submitted an application stating that the sole plaintiff was dead, without stating the date of death. He further stated that as his power to work as the advocate for the plaintiff had ceased, he was unable to take any step in the case. The learned Munsif fixed 16- 4-76 as the date of positive hearing of the suit. On the said date no steps were taken by the plaintiff and hence the learned Munsif dismissed the suit for default. 

 3. On 9-6-76 the present petitioners as heirs and successors of the deceased plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.191 of 1976 under Order 9, Rule 4 read with Section 151 C.P.C. praying for setting aside the order dated 16-4-76 and for restoration of the suit. By his judgment and order dated 26-6-76 the learned Munsif dismissed the Miscellaneous case as not maintainable on the ground that the application was filed more than 30 days after the date of dismissal for default and as such it was barred by limitation. 

 4. Mr. Md. Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case the learned Munsif ought to have taken into consideration that had there been no dismissal for default, the petitioners were still within time in filing an application for substitution of the heirs and successors of the deceased plaintiff. He submits that the learned Munsif should have treated the petitioners, application under Order 9, Rule 4 C.P.C. as basically an application for substitution and should have corrected the erroneous order dated 16-4-76 passed in ignorance of the date of death of the sole plaintiff. Mr. Chaklader submits that this is a fit and proper case where in the interest of justice the learned Munsif should have exercised his powers under section 151 C.P.C 

 3. Procedure in case of death of one of several plaintiffs or of sole plaintiff. 

 7. The only order that the learned Munsif could have passed in the present case after being informed of the death of the sole plaintiff was to record an abatement of the suit. He has no jurisdiction to fix the suit for positive hearing on 16-4-76. When the petitioners filed the present Misc. Case on 9-6-76 they were still within time for substitution under Order 22 Rule 3 C.P.C. Once the fact of the date of death of the deceased plaintiff was known to the learned Munsif and the date was not controverted, he ought to have realised that the earlier order of dismissal for default was wholly without jurisdiction. He should have retraced his steps under section 151 C.P.C. 

 8. I find support for my views in a decision of the Privy Council. In the case of Raja Debi Baksh Singh V. Habib shah XVIII (1913) C.L.J (P.C) 9 the facts were that the plaintiff was dead and it was unknown to the Judge who dismissed the suit for non-appearance of the plaintiff. The deceased plaintiff s son applied within the period of limitation to have his name substituted in place of his deceased father under Order 22, Rule 3 C.P.C. It was held by the Privy Council that the Rules or Orders of the Code dealing with the case of non-appearance of a suitor were inapplicable to a situation when the suitor was dead. Upon being pointed out the mistake it was the duty of the Court to rectify it. The application for substitution should have been granted and the suit should have been proceeded with, It was also held that quite apart from section 151 C.P.C. the Court possesses an inherent power to rectify the mistake which had been inadvertently committed, but that section could be properly invoked and apart from points of procedure and otherwise, should be taken advantage of. It was further held that "the principle of forfeiture rights in consequence of a default in procedure by a party to a cause is a principle of punishment in respect of such default, but the punishment of the dead or the ranking of death under the category of default does not seem to be very stateable. 

 9. The learned Munsif therefore should have accepted the application of the petitioners dated 9-6-76 as basically an application under Order 22 Rule 3 C.P.C. He ought to have set aside his order dated 16-4-76 and should have restored the suit and after substituting the petitioners as plaintiffs should have proceeded with the trial thereof. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 26-6-76 passed by the learned Munsif in Miscellaneous Case No. 191 of 1976 is set aside. The order dated 16-4-76 passed by the learned Munsif dismissing Title Suit No.4 of 1974 for default of the plaintiff is also set aside and the said suit is restored to its file and number. The petitioners are substituted as plaintiffs of the said suit as the legal heirs and successors of the deceased plaintiff in pursuance of their application dated 9.6.76, subject to any just exception that may be taken by the defendant-opposite party at the time of trial. The learned Munsif is directed to proceed with the trial of the said suit.
